abstract: Lithium-manganese-rich cathodes offer exceptional theoretical capacities but suffer from manganese dissolution/deposition, which limits performance. This work demonstrates that first-cycle electrochemical reduction can be modulated through electrolyte chemistry and applied C-rate. We show that solid-electrolyte <mark>interphase</mark> passivation quality is not an inherent guarantee of the reduction process, but rather a variable outcome of the specific electrochemical pathways triggered.
